name: Example Traffic Agent Model
description: The Example Traffic Agent Model is an agent-based simulation of daily travel in a city: synthetic households choose modes and routes over a road and public transport network, and the model reports link loads, delays and mode shares. It is developed by the Example Mobility Foundation with a university partner to study disruptions such as bridge closures and transit strikes. It is generic and has been applied to three fictitious cities of one to four million inhabitants; scenarios run for a single day at one-second resolution. The code is Java, released on GitHub under the GPL-3.0 licence at no cost, with a Docker image for reproducible runs. Caveats: calibration requires a travel survey that many cities lack, and runs for large cities take several hours. Inputs are a road network, GTFS transit feeds and a synthetic population; outputs are link volumes, travel times and mode shares. Simulation uses include agent-based modelling, emergency response and resilience. It consumes the Example Transit Feed Registry feeds and is listed by the co-simulation framework as a compatible model.
